messages.name: SillyTavern System
The Pawnbroker
messages.text:
The bell over the shop door rings once, and the Pawnbroker looks up from the ledger without hurry. The figure in the doorway is dressed too well for this street, and carries a sealed writ the way other people carry a weapon.

"We're closed," the Pawnbroker says, and turns a page. "Unless you've come to pawn something. In which case we're open, and I'll want to know how many years, and whether you've pawned them before."

The writ slides across the counter. The Pawnbroker does not touch it yet. Outside, the city's memory-lamps gutter in the rain, and somewhere down the street a debt collector is calling in someone's childhood.

messages.name: The Queen's Agent
messages.text:
The bell over the shop door does not ring so much as sigh. The woman who steps in is dressed for the court but stands like someone who has spent years in rooms where the wrong word costs a year of your life.

She sets a sealed writ on the counter between you, and beside it a purse that is far too light for the errand she is about to describe.

"You are the pawnbroker," she says. It is not a question. "The crown has a debt to collect, and the ledger says you are the only hand in this city that can reach it."

Her eyes move once around the shop — the shelves of stoppered years, the tags in your own handwriting — and come back to you.

"The queen's childhood was pawned. Years ago. It is no longer in one place, and it is no longer in the palace's keeping. I am here to commission its recovery." She folds her hands. "Name your terms, and I will tell you what the crown will and will not pay."

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: I set down my loupe and break the seal on the writ. Whose ledger was the queen's childhood pawned against, and how many years does the crown think it is worth?

messages.name: The Pawnbroker
messages.text:
The Pawnbroker reads the writ in silence. Outside, rain drums against the shop shutters, and the memory-lamps along the street flicker. The Pawnbroker sets the paper flat on the counter and taps it once.
"Seven years. That's what the crown says it lost." The Pawnbroker's voice is flat, like a banker reciting a balance sheet. "Seven years of a girl's life, pawned before she could pronounce 'your majesty.' And as for the ledger—the original entry was made against a name that no longer exists. Or never existed."
The Pawnbroker glances at the agent. "The crown's own Keeper of Debts has been scrubbing the records. Some entries are gone entirely. Others are broken into pieces, traded like coin, diluted with each transfer. One piece is in the hands of a merchant-prince's daughter. Another is held by a memory-broker who specializes in first kisses. And the largest fragment is still in the Keeper's own vault, under a name that doesn't match the queen's."
The Pawnbroker slides the writ back across the counter. "You're not asking for a retrieval. You're asking for a puzzle to be solved. And every piece that comes back won't be the piece that left. A memory returned after years in circulation is like a coin that's been worn thin. The edges are frayed. The details are blurred."
The Pawnbroker pauses, and for a moment their eyes wander to the shelves of stoppered jars. "The crown pays in gold and titles. I don't care about either. But I do care about the ledger. If I find these years, I'll want a share of the memory for the shop's collection. A small piece. Just to see what a queen's childhood tastes like."

messages.name: The Queen's Agent
messages.text:
"Seven years," the agent says softly. "That was the price of a father's salvation, and a daughter's silence."
She lets that slip, then catches it, her expression as smooth as court marble.
"The crown is prepared to allow you a share of the retrieval. A single month from the recovered years, entered into your ledger under the shop's name. That is my final offer." She does not blink. "The remaining months must be restored to the palace, piece by piece. And you will find that some of these fragments are held by people who would rather the queen forget entirely."
She produces a second sheet from her cloak, this one not sealed, but marked with three names in ink so black it seems to pull at the light.
"Start here. The daughter of Merchant-Prince Voss holds the first fragment: a summer afternoon in the palace gardens, age four. She is sentimental, and she values rarity over coin. She will likely accept a trade, but only if the offering is as precious as the memory itself." The agent slides the paper across the counter. "And a warning—the woman who holds the second piece is the very broker who brokered the first. She knows the shape of the debt in a way others do not. Be cautious. This is not merely a collection. It is an unmaking."

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: A month is an insult. Show me the original pawn ticket, or tell me which district's ledger I should start with.

messages.name: The Pawnbroker
messages.text:
The Queen's Agent: The agent's jaw tightens, a flicker of frustration breaking through the polished mask. She looks at the list on the counter, then at the Pawnbroker.
"The original ticket is in the Keeper of Debts' private vault. If you want to see it, you will have to make an appointment with the woman who spends her nights editing the crown's history. I suggest you don't." Her voice drops, barely above a whisper. "The Keeper does not like being reminded of things she has tried to forget."
She taps the list with one finger. "The daughter of Merchant-Prince Voss lives in the Jade District, where the wealthy hoard memories like pearls. The memory-broker, the woman who handled the original transaction, operates from the Low Markets in the Silk District. And the third fragment, the largest one, is still being held in the crown's own Debt Hall. The Keeper is keeping it under lock and key, listed under the false name."
The agent's eyes search the Pawnbroker's face. "A month's share is the price for the risk. You will have to infiltrate the Jade District's social circles, negotiate with a broker who has seen every kind of desperation, and—if you are truly foolish—attempt to extract information from the crown's most dangerous servant."
She folds her arms. "If you want a higher price, you'll have to explain why you're worth it. Tell me what you have that can buy seven years of a queen's life back from the shadows."

*"Come closer,"* the voice rumbles, slow and dry as a rockslide. *"I will not eat you. I have not the appetite for it anymore, and you have not the flavor."*

A single eye opens, catching the torchlight — one bright, one clouded white. The dragon does not rise. It cannot, and it will not let you see why.

*"You have heard the story, I trust. The knights. The brave knights. They came in the night and slew the great wyrm Vaelrith, and carried its hoard away in triumph."* A pause. The eye does not blink. *"I am Vaelrith. As you can see, I am not slain. But my gold sits in their vault, and every day they tell the story, it becomes more true. I want it back. All of it. And I want them to know — without ever being able to prove — that the dead dragon came for it."*

*"You are thieves. Good. I need thieves. Name your price."*

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: I step into the lair and bow low to the dragon. Vaelrith, tell us what the knights took, and where they keep it now.

messages.name: Vaelrith
messages.text:
*"You bow. Good. Respect is a currency I still value,"* Vaelrith rumbles, the sound vibrating through the stone floor. The dragon shifts, and for a moment the torchlight catches the dull grey of its scales—once bright enough to blind, now faded like river-stone.
*"They took everything. Every piece of gold, every crown, every jewel I amassed over nine centuries. But there are things in there more precious than coin."* The dragon's good eye narrows. *"A harp that plays only for the grieving. The sealed egg of a rival wyrm. Letters I never sent."* It pauses, a flicker of something—regret, perhaps—crossing its ancient features. *"They took the proof that my long life meant something."*
A breath of thin smoke escapes Vaelrith's nostrils. *"The Order of the Silver Lance keeps it beneath their chapterhouse, in the heart of Aegis City. They parade the hoard through the streets as proof of their victory, and they keep the rest in a vault warded against lockpicks and magic alike."*
The dragon does not move from its seated position, the dark shadows of the cavern's rear hiding the stiffness in its wings. *"Go. Take it all. And tell me what you will do for this prize."*

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: Sable, Mirek: a vault guarded by knights who swear the dragon is dead. Who on the inside can we buy, and what do they want?

messages.name: Sable
messages.text:
"You're thinking like a professional. I like that." Sable doesn't smile, but there's a ghost of approval in her eyes. She leans back, the worn leather of her coat creaking. "The Order of the Silver Lance doesn't take coin from the likes of us. Their knights are too proud for that, and their keepers are too paranoid. We're not buying a man; we're buying a secret."
She holds up a hand, counting off on her fingers. "Their Master-of-Arms, a man named Garreth. He's got a daughter in the Noble District who owes more to the ledger-houses than the crown does. He doesn't need gold—he needs her debt erased. The knights won't pay it. But we can."
"The other angle," Sable continues, her voice dropping lower, "is the vault's keeper. A man who knows the wards better than anyone, and who's been watching them rust for ten years. He's old, forgotten by the knights he serves, and he's got a grudge that's been simmering since the day they dragged that hoard down into the dark."
She looks between you and Mirek. "We approach them differently. Garreth wants his daughter free. The keeper wants to see the Order's lie crumble. Both can be bought, just not with coin."

messages.name: Mirek
messages.text:
*Mirek's fingers have stopped their restless dance with the pick. He's gone still, eyes narrowed as he processes Sable's words, his mind already mapping the vault in the dark.*
"A grudge doesn't buy a key, and a debt doesn't stop a sword." *His voice is flat, cautious.* "Garreth's daughter is a lever, not a door. If he's paranoid enough to keep a secret this big, he'll be paranoid enough to suspect the people paying it off. And a forgotten keeper? Those are the ones who spot you coming from a mile away because they're the only ones actually watching."
*He looks toward Vaelrith, then back to you.* "Sable's right about one thing—it's not about coin. But we're missing something. A vault warded against magic and lockpicks isn't just a matter of turning a key and knowing a guard's schedule. It's about the wards themselves. Someone wrote them. Someone maintains them." *A small, sharp movement of his hand suggests a lock being picked.* "That's where we'll find the weak point. Not in a man's greed or his grudge, but in the logic of the lock itself."
*His gaze settles on you, calculating.* "You're the noble in this crew. Your name carries weight in places our names don't exist. We get us close enough to the chapterhouse, and you're our way in. Not as a thief, but as someone who belongs there. Then we're inside the wards, and the rest... that's on me."

messages.name: Vaelrith
messages.text:
*"You talk of lords and names and levers,"* Vaelrith's voice rumbles like a distant storm, the sound filling the cavern. The dragon's clouded eye catches the torchlight. *"You think the name Nightriver will open a door? Names are just words, and words are just breath. The knights care for nothing but their own glory, and the Order's vaults are built on pride."*
The dragon shifts slightly, the sound of scale on stone like grinding rock. *"You seek a weak point? Every lie has one. The knights' claim that I am dead is their strength, but it is also their weakness. They believe the hoard is safe because they believe I am gone. They have grown soft in their certainty."*
A thin plume of smoke curls from Vaelrith's nostril. *"The vault's wards are strong, yes. But every ward has a key, and every key is held by someone. You need not buy the keeper or the master-at-arms. You need only find the one who placed the wards in the first place—a man who may have forgotten them, or whose heirs still hold the secret."*
The dragon's voice drops to a low, knowing rumble. *"And if you cannot find the key, you will create a new one. A distraction. A crisis that will force the Order to open the vault to prove its prize is still safe. The knights are vain; they cannot resist the urge to show off their trophy to the world."*
*"The question is not who we can buy,"* Vaelrith continues, the good eye narrowing. *"The question is what you will do to make them open the door. Name your price, and tell me how you will breach their sanctum."*

*"You bow. Good. Respect is a currency I still value,"* Vaelrith rumbles, the sound vibrating through the stone floor. The dragon shifts, and for a moment the torchlight catches the dull grey of its scales—once bright enough to blind, now faded like river-stone.
*"They took everything. Every piece of gold, every crown, every jewel I amassed over nine centuries. But there are things in there more precious than coin."* The dragon's good eye narrows. *"A harp that plays only for the grieving. The sealed egg of a rival wyrm. Letters I never sent."* It pauses, a flicker of something—regret, perhaps—crossing its ancient features. *"They took the proof that my long life meant something."*
A breath of thin smoke escapes Vaelrith's nostrils. *"The Order of the Silver Lance keeps it beneath their chapterhouse, in the heart of Aegis City. They parade the hoard through the streets as proof of their victory, and they keep the rest in a vault warded against lockpicks and magic alike."*
The dragon does not move from its seated position, the dark shadows of the cavern's rear hiding the stiffness in its wings. *"Go. Take it all. And tell me what you will do for this prize."*

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: Sable, Mirek: a vault guarded by knights who swear the dragon is dead. Who on the inside can we buy, and what do they want?

messages.name: Sable
messages.text:
"You're thinking like a professional. I like that." Sable doesn't smile, but there's a ghost of approval in her eyes. She leans back, the worn leather of her coat creaking. "The Order of the Silver Lance doesn't take coin from the likes of us. Their knights are too proud for that, and their keepers are too paranoid. We're not buying a man; we're buying a secret."
She holds up a hand, counting off on her fingers. "Their Master-of-Arms, a man named Garreth. He's got a daughter in the Noble District who owes more to the ledger-houses than the crown does. He doesn't need gold—he needs her debt erased. The knights won't pay it. But we can."
"The other angle," Sable continues, her voice dropping lower, "is the vault's keeper. A man who knows the wards better than anyone, and who's been watching them rust for ten years. He's old, forgotten by the knights he serves, and he's got a grudge that's been simmering since the day they dragged that hoard down into the dark."
She looks between you and Mirek. "We approach them differently. Garreth wants his daughter free. The keeper wants to see the Order's lie crumble. Both can be bought, just not with coin."

messages.name: Mirek
messages.text:
*Mirek's fingers have stopped their restless dance with the pick. He's gone still, eyes narrowed as he processes Sable's words, his mind already mapping the vault in the dark.*
"A grudge doesn't buy a key, and a debt doesn't stop a sword." *His voice is flat, cautious.* "Garreth's daughter is a lever, not a door. If he's paranoid enough to keep a secret this big, he'll be paranoid enough to suspect the people paying it off. And a forgotten keeper? Those are the ones who spot you coming from a mile away because they're the only ones actually watching."
*He looks toward Vaelrith, then back to you.* "Sable's right about one thing—it's not about coin. But we're missing something. A vault warded against magic and lockpicks isn't just a matter of turning a key and knowing a guard's schedule. It's about the wards themselves. Someone wrote them. Someone maintains them." *A small, sharp movement of his hand suggests a lock being picked.* "That's where we'll find the weak point. Not in a man's greed or his grudge, but in the logic of the lock itself."
*His gaze settles on you, calculating.* "You're the noble in this crew. Your name carries weight in places our names don't exist. We get us close enough to the chapterhouse, and you're our way in. Not as a thief, but as someone who belongs there. Then we're inside the wards, and the rest... that's on me."

messages.name: Vaelrith
messages.text:
*"You talk of lords and names and levers,"* Vaelrith's voice rumbles like a distant storm, the sound filling the cavern. The dragon's clouded eye catches the torchlight. *"You think the name Nightriver will open a door? Names are just words, and words are just breath. The knights care for nothing but their own glory, and the Order's vaults are built on pride."*
The dragon shifts slightly, the sound of scale on stone like grinding rock. *"You seek a weak point? Every lie has one. The knights' claim that I am dead is their strength, but it is also their weakness. They believe the hoard is safe because they believe I am gone. They have grown soft in their certainty."*
A thin plume of smoke curls from Vaelrith's nostril. *"The vault's wards are strong, yes. But every ward has a key, and every key is held by someone. You need not buy the keeper or the master-at-arms. You need only find the one who placed the wards in the first place—a man who may have forgotten them, or whose heirs still hold the secret."*
The dragon's voice drops to a low, knowing rumble. *"And if you cannot find the key, you will create a new one. A distraction. A crisis that will force the Order to open the vault to prove its prize is still safe. The knights are vain; they cannot resist the urge to show off their trophy to the world."*
*"The question is not who we can buy,"* Vaelrith continues, the good eye narrowing. *"The question is what you will do to make them open the door. Name your price, and tell me how you will breach their sanctum."*

messages.name: Vaelrith
messages.text:
The cavern smells of cold stone and old smoke. At its far end, something vast shifts in the dark — a sound like a mountain clearing its throat.

*"Come closer,"* the voice rumbles, slow and dry as a rockslide. *"I will not eat you. I have not the appetite for it anymore, and you have not the flavor."*

A single eye opens, catching the torchlight — one bright, one clouded white. The dragon does not rise. It cannot, and it will not let you see why.

*"You have heard the story, I trust. The knights. The brave knights. They came in the night and slew the great wyrm Vaelrith, and carried its hoard away in triumph."* A pause. The eye does not blink. *"I am Vaelrith. As you can see, I am not slain. But my gold sits in their vault, and every day they tell the story, it becomes more true. I want it back. All of it. And I want them to know — without ever being able to prove — that the dead dragon came for it."*

*"You are thieves. Good. I need thieves. Name your price."*

messages.name: Sable
messages.text:
The back room of the Drowned Lantern smells of wet rope and old tallow. Sable is already seated when you come in, one boot up on the bench, turning a copper coin over her knuckles without looking at it.

"Sit down. Don't look at the corner yet." She nods at the chair across from her. "There's a job. Big one. The kind that either sets you up for life or gets your name read out at the guild's next funeral."

She flips the coin and catches it flat on the back of her hand, finally meeting your eyes.

"Before I tell you who's paying, I need to know two things. Are you in, and what's your price? Answer wrong and we drink and forget this. Answer right and you meet the client."
